-118.41470,34.06240.name: Beverly Hills Fertility
-118.41470,34.06240.desc: A fertility clinic reporting to the CDC's National ART Surveillance System. Medical director: Ellen Goldstein, MD. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. Reporting is required of every US clinic performing assisted reproduction, under the Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act, so this is close to a complete register rather than a list of members. What it records is cycles started, which is not the same as children born.

-81.79473,26.15349.name: Harmony Health Clinic
-81.79473,26.15349.desc: A clinic mapped in OpenStreetMap as offering fertility treatment. Operated by Dr Joshua Lamers. OpenStreetMap holds what somebody chose to map, so a country with few points here may be thinly mapped rather than thinly served. That is the reverse of the national registers alongside it, which are close to complete for one country and silent everywhere else. This layer is a cross-check and a source of leads, not a count.

-122.15985,37.44433.name: Palo Alto Health Care System
-122.15985,37.44433.desc: An organisation accredited by AAALAC International for its care and use of laboratory animals. Part of Department of Veterans Affairs. Accreditation is voluntary and paid for, so this is a list of organisations that chose to be inspected rather than a register of everyone doing the work. An organisation absent from it is not accredited; that says nothing about whether it uses animals. In several countries the largest users are absent for exactly that reason. The directory gives a city and country and no street address, so this point marks where the organisation is registered rather than the building where animals are held.

-2.57959,51.45564.name: London Women's Clinic, Bristol
-2.57959,51.45564.state: Zinc Works, 2 Unity Road, Bristol, BS2 0NX
-2.57959,51.45564.company: Satellite clinic to London Women's Clinic
-2.57959,51.45564.desc: A fertility clinic licensed and inspected by the Human Fertilisation and Embryology Authority. Satellite clinic to London Women's Clinic. A satellite is where patients are seen; the licence sits with the parent clinic, so the regulator's paperwork and the treatment are in different places. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. The HFEA licenses every clinic in the United Kingdom, inspects them, and publishes findings and success rates clinic by clinic. No other fertility regulator publishes at this level, which makes the UK the one country where this sector can be read rather than estimated.

-71.05213,48.41870.name: Université du Québec à Chicoutimi
-71.05213,48.41870.status: Certificate of GAP Last visit: regular, October 2023
-71.05213,48.41870.desc: An institution certified by the Canadian Council on Animal Care for its use of animals in science. Certificate of GAP Last visit: regular, October 2023. CCAC certification is a condition of federal research funding rather than a licence, so an institution outside it is not necessarily outside the work — it may simply not take federal money. The CCAC publishes names and certificate status and no addresses, so this point marks the institution rather than the building where animals are held.

-6.25000,53.35000.name: Teagasc
-6.25000,53.35000.desc: Ireland’s state agriculture and food development authority, running research and advisory services for a livestock-dominated agriculture. State advisory bodies decide what reaches farmers as recommendation rather than as sales pitch, and in countries that still have them, they are the main counterweight to the input suppliers’ own agronomists.

7.60100,47.56200.name: Roche / Genentech
7.60100,47.56200.desc: Genentech was the first biotechnology company and is now inside Roche, which also owns one of the largest diagnostics businesses in the world. A company that sells both the test and the treatment for the same condition occupies a position competition authorities have blocked elsewhere, most recently in Illumina’s case.

145.79000,-5.22000.name: National Agricultural Research Institute — Papua New Guinea
145.79000,-5.22000.desc: New Guinea is a centre of origin for sugarcane, banana and taro, and one of the most biologically diverse places on Earth. Its national research institute is small, its collections are globally significant, and the mismatch between those two facts is the ordinary condition of centres of origin.

-77.03280,38.88780.name: USDA Agricultural Mediation Program
-77.03280,38.88780.state: Washington DC — USDA, 1400 Independence Avenue SW
-77.03280,38.88780.desc: Free or nearly free mediation between farmers and neighbours, lenders and agencies, funded federally and run by the states. It is faster than a court, produces a written agreement, and does not require either side to be found at fault. For a dispute between neighbouring growers — which is what most drift is — it is usually the first thing to try, because a court case between people who will farm beside each other for thirty years has costs a judgment does not settle.
